//: A WORKED EXAMPLE of a white-label, committed so the exit gate can be demonstrated rather than described. `docs/126` phase 3 asks for a build that is white-labelled with no code changes and still passes the contrast sweep — so this file is a real host configuration, `tests/brand.test.mjs` generates from it and audits the result, and `tests/e2e/white-label.spec.mjs` installs the stylesheet it produces into a real editor and runs the full contrast sweep over both themes. Copy it over `brand.json` to white-label a deployment.
//name: Not a real company. A plausible one: a fictional host, so nothing here impersonates anybody.
name: Northwind Docs

theme.//: A deliberately DIFFERENT palette from ours, because a guard that passes because the default theme is applied proves nothing. The accent is a deep teal and the greys are warmer than ours; every value was checked against the floors by the generator rather than picked by eye, and two of the first three attempts were refused (see the PR).

strings.//: Nothing here renames the product — `name` already does that in all nineteen languages, derived from the catalogues. This is the escape hatch for a host who wants different words in a particular language, and it wins over the derived override.

de.branding.themeSetByHost: Die Farbe wird von Northwind Docs vorgegeben.
